learningObjectives: Select and justify keyed data pages in a business scenario.
reviewScope: Official topic comparison and original-question editorial review; not vendor endorsement.

elements.description: A keyed Data Page selects embedded records from one cached list using configured keys, reducing repeated source calls for individual items. Keyed access is supported for read-only pages with thread or requestor scope. Define keys, uniqueness and refresh strategy; keyed access is not a guarantee that a stale or incomplete source list contains every current record.

elements.text: Worked example: A requestor-scoped product list is loaded once, keyed by ProductID, and supplies details for multiple selections. Refresh the list when the business requires newer catalog data; compare connector calls before and after the change.

elements.title: Training environment checklist
items: Implement the worked example in a training application; use synthetic data.
Test the expected path and at least one failure or boundary condition.
Explain why the alternative mechanism would not meet the requirement.
Revisit incorrect answers in Smart Review rather than memorizing option positions.

elements.text: These notes target the '25 exam. Shared Academy pages may show newer labels with '25 applicability; verify screens in your training environment.

examPitfalls.title: Key versus connector parameter
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Every keyed lookup requires a new remote request.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Lookup uses records in the cached list subject to its load/refresh policy.

examPitfalls.title: Cache versus freshness
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configure refresh according to business requirements.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A form loads a list of branches, then retrieves several branch details by ID. What can reduce repeated source calls?

options.text: Make the list a Product rule
Enable keyed access on the cached list Data Page
Create a new connector per branch label

practiceQuiz.rationale: Keyed access retrieves matching embedded records from the list. It can avoid separate detail pages and repeated source exchanges.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO scopes support keyed access on a read-only Data Page?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Keyed Data Pages support read-only thread and requestor scopes. Do not assume the same keyed-access configuration supports node scope.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Data Page mode is supported for this keyed-access configuration?
practiceQuiz.rationale: This feature selects records from a read-only list. Editing and saving use different data management mechanisms.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The source list changed after it was cached. Why may a keyed lookup return outdated data?

options.text: Requestor pages never load from connectors
Keyed lookup does not itself guarantee a reload of the source list
Every key lookup deletes the cache

practiceQuiz.rationale: Caching and freshness are separate requirements. Apply an appropriate refresh strategy to the source list.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Two records share the supposed unique lookup key. What should the team review?

options.text: The key design and uniqueness of the source data

practiceQuiz.rationale: A deterministic single-record lookup needs suitable keys. Duplicate identifiers undermine that assumption.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which measurement best checks the expected benefit of keyed access?

options.text: Source calls while selecting several records from the same loaded list
The number of case stages only
The pass score of a mock exam

practiceQuiz.rationale: The proposed improvement is fewer exchanges with the source, so measure those calls for a representative sequence.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A required record is absent from a cached filtered list. What is the safe conclusion?

options.text: The record cannot exist in any source
It must be a locking failure
The lookup list may not cover that record; review filtering and refresh

practiceQuiz.rationale: A lookup operates on available cached records. Absence from that subset is not proof of absence from the authoritative system.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A list is keyed by warehouse and item ID. Which input must the lookup provide?

options.text: Values for the configured key fields

practiceQuiz.rationale: Configured keys identify the relevant record. Unrelated metadata cannot select the business row.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.
